summary: Magan Airport (GYG/UEMM) is a regional airport serving the settlement of Magan in the Sakha Republic (Yakutia), Russian Far East. Located just southwest of Yakutsk, it functions as a secondary airfield supporting regional flights in one of the world's coldest inhabited regions. The airport handles smaller turboprop aircraft suited to the extreme subarctic climate, where winter temperatures routinely drop below -40°C.
faqs:
Q: Where is Magan Airport located relative to Yakutsk?
A: Magan Airport is situated approximately 10 km southwest of Yakutsk, the capital of the Sakha Republic, serving as a secondary airfield in the metropolitan area.

Q: What type of aircraft typically operates at Magan Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves smaller regional aircraft and turboprops suited to short-haul flights within Yakutia, rather than large commercial jets.

Q: Is Magan Airport open year-round despite the extreme cold?
A: Yes, the airport operates year-round, though winter operations require specialized cold-weather procedures and equipment common to airports in the Sakha Republic.

Q: Does Magan Airport handle international flights?
A: No, Magan is a domestic regional airport; international traffic for the region is handled through Yakutsk Airport (YKS).
transport_tips: The airport is a short drive from Yakutsk city center, typically reachable in 15-20 minutes by car or taxi depending on road and weather conditions. In winter, allow extra time as icy roads and extreme cold can slow travel. Public transport options are limited, so arranging a taxi in advance is recommended, especially during the long winter months.
local_tip: If flying out in winter, dress in heavy layers and arrive early—Magan and the broader Yakutsk region experience some of the most severe cold snaps on Earth, and even short walks between terminals or to parking areas can be brutally cold.
